doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Drafted into the Fredonia big band
summary: He is put in the big band without an audition, as the only black member, which he reads as stereotyping.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Everybody, we shared a house together. So anyway it was cool but there was still this thing because I was drafted into the big band. You know, usually every situation you have to audition, you have to go through a whole process. And I have to admit it was very weird. Because I was called to the rehearsal and they said, “Well sit down at the piano and start playing.” And they said well it’s like, “You got the gig.” I said, “Excuse me? I just got here.” It was like not to make it seem too — I don’t know how to put it — but it was almost like a situation where okay you’re black, you’re from New York, you play jazz, we need a piano player.
